title: Signature Literal and metacharacter basics — Regular Expression Search
description: Signature original — A regex is a pattern where most characters match themselves and metacharacters like . * + ? carry special meaning. Escaping with a backslash turns a metacharacter back into a literal, so '\.' matches a real period. Knowing exactly which characters are special in the engine at hand prevents the most common pattern bugs. This record documents a Signature-authored original method of the JAH archive toolkit, clearly labeled as Signature work rather than a public record.
demo:
# Regex search: compile the pattern once, scan each line, report matches with spans.
import re
text = """see archive.txt and archive_txt here"""
pattern = r"archive\.txt"
rx = re.compile(pattern)
print("Pattern:", pattern)
found = False
for i, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
    for m in rx.finditer(line):
        found = True
        print(f"line {i} [{m.start()}:{m.end()}]: {m.group(0)!r}")
if not found:
    print("no matches")
provenance: Signature-authored original method created for the JAH archive toolkit; clearly labeled Signature, not a public record.

title: Signature Character classes — Regular Expression Search
description: Signature original — Bracket expressions like [0-9] or [a-zA-Z] match any single character from the listed set. Negated classes [^0-9] match anything outside the set, and shorthands like \d, \w, \s cover the everyday cases. Classes keep patterns readable where alternations of single characters would sprawl. title: Signature Quantifiers: greedy and lazy — Regular Expression Search
description: Signature original — Quantifiers *, +, ?, and {m,n} repeat the preceding atom; by default they are greedy, consuming as much as possible. Appending ? makes them lazy, matching as little as possible, which changes what '<.*>' captures in '<a><b>'. Choosing greedy versus lazy correctly is the difference between one big match and many small ones. This record documents a Signature-authored original method of the JAH archive toolkit, clearly labeled as Signature work rather than a public record.

title: Signature Anchors and boundaries — Regular Expression Search
description: Signature original — The anchors ^ and $ pin a match to the start or end of the string (or line, in multiline mode). The word boundary \b sits between word and non-word characters, so '\bcat\b' skips 'catalog'. Anchors turn substring search into whole-field validation, the basis of input checking. This record documents a Signature-authored original method of the JAH archive toolkit, clearly labeled as Signature work rather than a public record.

title: Signature Groups and capturing — Regular Expression Search
description: Signature original — Parentheses group atoms for quantification and alternation, and by default they also capture the matched text. Numbered backreferences \1, \2 reuse a captured group later in the same pattern, enabling duplicate-word detection. Non-capturing groups (?:...) give the grouping without the bookkeeping overhead. This record documents a Signature-authored original method of the JAH archive toolkit, clearly labeled as Signature work rather than a public record.

title: Signature Alternation — Regular Expression Search
description: Signature original — The pipe a|b tries the left branch first and falls back to the right, scoped by the enclosing group. Ordering matters: 'cat|catalog' on 'catalog' matches just 'cat' unless the longer branch comes first or a boundary is added. Alternation is how patterns express synonyms and spelling variants in one pass. This record documents a Signature-authored original method of the JAH archive toolkit, clearly labeled as Signature work rather than a public record.

title: Signature Backreferences and lookarounds — Regular Expression Search
description: Signature original — Lookahead (?=...) and lookbehind (?<=...) assert context without consuming characters, so '\w+(?=:) ' finds labels. Negative variants (?!...) and (?<!...) assert absence, the regex way of saying 'not followed by'. These zero-width assertions add boolean-style conditions to otherwise linear patterns. This record documents a Signature-authored original method of the JAH archive toolkit, clearly labeled as Signature work rather than a public record.

title: Signature NFA simulation and backtracking — Regular Expression Search
description: Signature original — Most popular engines implement regexes as nondeterministic finite automata explored with backtracking. Backtracking tries one path, and on failure rewinds to the last choice point to try another, which is why nested quantifiers like '(a+)+$' can explode exponentially. Understanding backtracking explains catastrophic slowdowns and motivates possessive quantifiers and atomic groups. This record documents a Signature-authored original method of the JAH archive toolkit, clearly labeled as Signature work rather than a public record.

title: Signature DFA-based matching — Regular Expression Search
description: Signature original — DFA engines convert the pattern to a deterministic automaton once, then scan the text in guaranteed linear time. They give up backreferences and lookarounds but never suffer catastrophic backtracking. For untrusted patterns or huge inputs, linear-time engines are the safe choice. This record documents a Signature-authored original method of the JAH archive toolkit, clearly labeled as Signature work rather than a public record.

title: Signature Regex over large archives — Regular Expression Search
description: Signature original — Scanning terabytes with one regex is I/O-bound, so engines split work across chunks and stream matches without loading whole files. Pre-filters like trigram indexes skip chunks that cannot match, running the full regex only on candidates. This two-phase design is how code search tools stay fast over entire repositories. This record documents a Signature-authored original method of the JAH archive toolkit, clearly labeled as Signature work rather than a public record.

title: Signature Multiline and dotall modes — Regular Expression Search
description: Signature original — By default ^ and $ anchor to the whole string and . skips newlines; multiline mode makes anchors per-line and dotall lets . cross lines. Flags (or inline (?m), (?s)) switch these behaviors without rewriting the pattern. Choosing the right mode is essential when patterns span log entries or document sections. This record documents a Signature-authored original method of the JAH archive toolkit, clearly labeled as Signature work rather than a public record.

title: Signature Unicode character properties — Regular Expression Search
description: Signature original — Modern engines match by Unicode property, so '\p{L}+' finds letters in any script, not just ASCII. title: Signature From regex to index-assisted search — Regular Expression Search
description: Signature original — Trigram indexes extract all 3-character substrings of both the corpus and the pattern's required literals. Chunks lacking a required trigram are skipped without running the regex at all. This is how indexed code search answers regex queries over millions of files in under a second.
